source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
Because Cambodia's own animal feed manufacturing sector is still limited, and there are relatively few large domestic corn buyers/millers, national corn output has historically outpaced domestic consumption -- the surplus is exported to neighboring countries, mainly Thailand and Vietnam.

Estimated domestic corn demand (in thousand tons, cited to Barrientos 2017a), with year-on-year growth in parentheses: 2007: 300 (+200.0%); 2008: 350 (+16.7%); 2009: 700 (+100.0%); 2010: 600 (-14.3%); 2011: 500 (-16.7%); 2012: 700 (+40.0%); 2013: 600 (-14.3%); 2014: 450 (-25.0%); 2015: 500 (+11.1%); 2016: 550 (+10.0%).

Over the ten years to the document's writing, roughly 10 large-scale feed mills and about 100 smaller feed-mill operations had started domestic corn-buying operations in Cambodia. In 2016, the Betagro group was the largest feed-mill buyer, sourcing an estimated 200,000 tons of corn domestically in a year. New Hope was the second-largest, a Japanese-invested company, and China also had feed-mill investment in Cambodia starting in 2016; M's Pig Feed and Angkor Green also began domestic corn purchasing that year. Estimated total domestic feed-mill corn demand was about 700,000 tons/year, though not all is sourced from local farmers -- feed mills also import corn directly.
